claims.statement: agent/thread_ids.py is the single home for deterministic thread-id derivation, and every id is a cross-process routing contract that webhooks, the dashboard, and the reviewer each re-derive from the same external identifiers to find an existing thread, so changing a formula orphans live threads.

Thread ids are derived either as URL-namespaced UUIDv5 (Slack, PR-comment, reviewer, review-style, baby-sit-lock) via uuid.uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, key), or as a SHA-256-derived UUID (Linear and GitHub issue ids) via _sha256_uuid.
slack_thread_id keys a Slack thread on the string slack:{channel}:{timestamp}:{nonce}, so rotating the nonce changes the derived id for the same channel/timestamp.

reviewer_thread_id derives a reviewer thread from {owner}/{repo}/pr/{pr_number}/reviewer, a namespace distinct from pr_comment_thread_id's {owner}/{repo}/pr/{pr_number}, so a PR's reviewer thread and agent thread never collide.

For a PR branch Open SWE created, the GitHub PR-comment webhook recovers the original agent thread id with thread_id_from_branch (a UUID scan of the branch name) and only falls back to pr_comment_thread_id when the branch carries no embedded id.
The Linear webhook routes an issue to its thread via linear_issue_thread_id(issue_id), keeping redeliveries of the same issue on one thread.

resolve_slack_thread_id resolves a Slack location by first checking an explicit stored mapping, then searching existing threads by source_context metadata for that location, and only falls back to the deterministic slack_thread_id (then binds it) when nothing matches; it raises when more than one thread matches a location.

bind_slack_thread_id persists a Slack-location-to-thread mapping in the Store namespace (_SLACK_THREAD_MAP_NAMESPACE, channel) keyed by timestamp, refuses to overwrite a location already mapped to a different thread, and verifies the write persisted, enforcing that a Slack location maps to at most one Open SWE thread.

delete_slack_thread_associations detaches a Slack location by rewriting its mapping with a fresh nonce, which changes the next deterministically derived slack_thread_id so a reused location does not collide with the retired thread.
Reviewer threads are tagged in metadata with kind = REVIEWER_THREAD_KIND ('reviewer'), which lets metadata searches and completion handling distinguish reviewer state from normal agent Slack work.

dispatch_agent_run routes Slack, Linear, GitHub, dashboard, and background triggers through create_durable_run, whose default durability='sync' checkpoints before each step so a crash or recycle resumes from the last checkpoint.

The default multitask_strategy='interrupt' halts an active run with its sync checkpoint preserved and runs the new message with thread history, while background follow-ups can opt into enqueue; webhook triggers no longer need an in-process busy lock, although dashboard injection and Slack edits retain a Store queue.

create_durable_run attaches COMPLETION_WEBHOOK_URL only when RUN_COMPLETE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set and the URL is a non-loopback absolute HTTP(S) URL, degrading to no webhook with a warning otherwise so a platform-rejected webhook cannot poison every runs.create.

create_durable_run sets stream_resumable=True and the Protocol v3 run shape (compatibility marker, stream_mode set, stream_subgraphs) so a client such as the dashboard that attaches to a run it did not start can replay events and observe it as running.

The Store FIFO queue in thread_ops is retained for dashboard follow-up injection and Slack message edits; queue_message_for_thread caps it at MAX_QUEUED_MESSAGES, dropping oldest entries beyond the cap.

langgraph.json configures the checkpointer TTL with strategy 'delete', default_ttl 43200 minutes, and a 60-minute sweep interval, so durable checkpoints of dormant threads are deleted on the hourly sweep.

agent/store.py is the single sanctioned Store access path and enforces that a missing item reads as None while any other failure raises, so a store outage is not collapsed into an empty record; critical-path callers must wrap their own try/except to survive an outage.
TypedStore binds a namespace to a Pydantic model; get raises on an unreadable record while search/search_all skip and log a bad record so one corrupt entry cannot fail an entire listing.

ensure_sandbox_for_thread reuses a cached backend or reconnects with sandbox_id from thread metadata, creating a sandbox only when neither exists; an unreachable existing agent sandbox raises rather than being silently replaced, while a deleted sandbox is replaced.

The thread is bound to its sandbox_id in metadata only after the sandbox is created and initialized, then the backend is published to the per-thread proxy cache, so a run that dies earlier leaves no half-built id for the next run to adopt.

Thread-level model and repository settings are resolved once on the first run and snapshotted onto thread metadata under agent_settings; later profile edits by any participant do not reach the thread unless the snapshot is explicitly rewritten, such as by a per-run model override.
Thread settings are strictly normalized to the declared thread-level schema, cached for five minutes, and both read and write fail soft so settings storage never breaks a run.

Thread participants are stored in metadata as a key-per-person object (participant_logins / participant_emails) rather than a list, because JSONB containment only reaches inside objects, allowing a metadata search to match a single participant entry.

A Slack code channel is treated as one agent session spanning the whole channel and is keyed with the sentinel timestamp CODE_CHANNEL_SESSION_TS = '0'; is_code_channel_session returns true exactly when thread_ts equals that sentinel.

manage_code_channel binds the code channel's agent thread to (channel_id, CODE_CHANNEL_SESSION_TS) via bind_slack_thread_id and updates its source_context, so every message in the channel resolves to the one session thread.

When fetching Slack conversation context, a code channel session reads the whole channel with conversations.history (no thread ts) while a normal Slack thread reads only that thread with conversations.replies keyed by ts; the '0' sentinel is what switches the API method.
A code channel session has its own lifecycle status (processing, active, suspended, closed) set through set_session_status, distinct from LangGraph thread status.

Run input serializes authored requests in validated, escaped input-message envelopes and can prepend hashed person, channel, and system dynamic-context introductions; previously injected introductions are suppressed, but context hidden by summarization is eligible for reintroduction.
RunConfig is a tolerant, forward-compatible per-run configurable contract: unknown keys survive round-trip, only invalid fields are dropped during parsing, and only supplied fields are emitted.

SourceContext is durable thread metadata that preserves unknown supplied fields and parses malformed historical context as empty; thread metadata upsert keeps an existing opening context and title rather than repointing a conversation on later activity.

PostgreSQL is a distinct relational state owner: it uses the open_swe schema and transaction-scoped migrations guarded by a PostgreSQL advisory lock, while the pull_request_thread table permits many links but a partial unique index permits only one primary thread per pull request.

The desktop local checkpointer commits checkpoints to SQLite and imports legacy in-memory pickle checkpoints once; its completion marker is written only after successful copying, so an interrupted import safely retries at the next start.
Dashboard thread authorization reads LangGraph thread metadata: private threads are readable by their immutable owner or an administrator, but only the owner may prompt a private thread.
